proofs.proof_tex:
Put \(T_{ia}=\mathbf 1(Z_i=a)\) and \(p=n/N=1/K\).  Because \(K\geq2\) and \(N\geq K\), all denominators below are positive.  Under balanced complete randomization,
\[
 \mathbb E_Z T_{ia}=p,
 \qquad
 \mathbb E_Z(T_{ia}T_{ja})=\frac{n(n-1)}{N(N-1)}\quad(i\ne j),
\]
and, for \(a\ne b\),
\[
 \mathbb E_Z(T_{ia}T_{ib})=0,
 \qquad
 \mathbb E_Z(T_{ia}T_{jb})=\frac{n^2}{N(N-1)}\quad(i\ne j).
\]
These identities follow by counting fixed-size allocations, using Assumption \(\mathrm{ass{:}balanced\text{-}complete\text{-}randomization}\).  Write \(y_i^a=Y_i(a)-\bar Y(a)\), so that \(\sum_i y_i^a=0\), \(\sum_i(y_i^a)^2=(N-1)S_{aa}(Y)\), and \(\sum_i y_i^a y_i^b=(N-1)S_{ab}(Y)\).  The preceding indicator moments give
\[
 \operatorname{Var}_Z\{\widehat{\bar Y}(a)\mid Y\}
 =\frac{1}{n^2}\left[p(1-p)\sum_i(y_i^a)^2
 -\frac{p(1-p)}{N-1}\sum_{i\ne j}y_i^a y_j^a\right].
\]
Since \(\sum_{i\ne j}y_i^a y_j^a=-\sum_i(y_i^a)^2\), this equals
\[
 \frac{p(1-p)N}{n^2(N-1)}(N-1)S_{aa}(Y)
 =\left(\frac1n-\frac1N\right)S_{aa}(Y).
\]
For \(a\ne b\), the same calculation and \(\sum_{i\ne j}y_i^a y_j^b=-\sum_i y_i^a y_i^b\) yield
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \operatorname{Cov}_Z\{\widehat{\bar Y}(a),\widehat{\bar Y}(b)\mid Y\}
 &=\frac1{n^2}\left[-p^2\sum_i y_i^a y_i^b
 +\frac{p^2}{N-1}\sum_{i\ne j}y_i^a y_j^b\right]\\
 &=-\frac1N S_{ab}(Y).
 \end{aligned}
\]
Thus
\[
 \operatorname{Cov}_Z(\widehat{\bar Y}\mid Y)
 =\operatorname{diag}\left(\frac{S_{aa}(Y)}n\right)_{a\in\mathcal A}-\frac{S(Y)}N.
\]
Multiplication on the left and right by \(C\) and \(C^{\mathsf T}\), respectively, proves the displayed formula for \(\Sigma_C(Y)\).  Finally, Definition \(\mathrm{def{:}contrast\text{-}risk}\), cyclicity of trace, and \(H=C^{\mathsf T}WC\) give
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \rho_W(Y)
 &=\operatorname{tr}\!\left[H\left\{\operatorname{diag}\left(\frac{S_{aa}(Y)}n\right)_{a\in\mathcal A}-\frac{S(Y)}N\right\}\right]\\
 &=\sum_{a\in\mathcal A}\frac{H_{aa}S_{aa}(Y)}n
 -\frac1N\sum_{a,b\in\mathcal A}H_{ab}S_{ab}(Y).
 \end{aligned}
\]
Within \(\mathcal S_N(F)\), every diagonal \(S_{aa}(Y)\) is fixed by \(F_a\); hence only the off-diagonal cross-arm covariances depend on the completion.

First note that \(H=C^{\mathsf T}WC\succeq0\), because \(W\succeq0\).  Assumption \(\mathrm{ass{:}causal\text{-}contrast}\) also gives
\[
 H\mathbf 1_K=C^{\mathsf T}WC\mathbf 1_K=0.
\]
Consequently, for this \(H\), membership in \(\mathcal R_K\) is equivalent to \(H_{ab}\leq0\) for all \(a\ne b\).

We use the following elementary finite rearrangement argument.  If \(u_1\leq\cdots\leq u_N\), \(v_1\leq\cdots\leq v_N\), and \(\eta\in\mathfrak S_N\), then any inversion \(p<q\) with \(\eta(p)>\eta(q)\) can be removed.  The change in the paired sum is
\[
 \{u_pv_{\eta(q)}+u_qv_{\eta(p)}\}
 -\{u_pv_{\eta(p)}+u_qv_{\eta(q)}\}
 =(u_q-u_p)(v_{\eta(p)}-v_{\eta(q)})\geq0.
\]
Successively removing inversions proves
\[
 \sum_{i=1}^N u_i v_i\geq \sum_{i=1}^N u_i v_{\eta(i)}.
\]
Subtracting the fixed product of the two means shows that, among all pairings of two empirical marginals, their finite-population covariance is maximized by their common-rank pairing.  Applying this pairwise to every \(a<b\) gives
\[
 S_{ab}\{Y^{\uparrow}(F)\}\geq S_{ab}(Y)
 \qquad\text{for every }Y\in\mathcal S_N(F).
\]

By Lemma \(\mathrm{lem{:}complete\text{-}randomization\text{-}risk}\), the diagonal terms cancel between two completions.  Symmetry of \(H\) and \(S(Y)\) therefore gives the exact identity
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \rho_W\{Y^{\uparrow}(F)\}-\rho_W(Y)
 &=-\frac1N\sum_{a\ne b}H_{ab}
 \left[S_{ab}\{Y^{\uparrow}(F)\}-S_{ab}(Y)\right]\\
 &=\frac2N\sum_{a<b}(-H_{ab})
 \left[S_{ab}\{Y^{\uparrow}(F)\}-S_{ab}(Y)\right].
 \end{aligned}
\]
If \(H\in\mathcal R_K\), every factor in the last sum is nonnegative, proving universal optimality and the claimed regret formula.

Conversely, suppose \(H\notin\mathcal R_K\).  The positive-semidefinite and zero-row-sum properties already proved imply that some pair \(a<b\) satisfies \(H_{ab}>0\).  Fix any \(N\) divisible by \(2K\), and let arms \(a\) and \(b\) each have \(N/2\) zeros and \(N/2\) ones, while every other arm is identically zero.  These are equal-weight empirical marginals.  Their common-rank covariance is
\[
 S_{ab}\{Y^{\uparrow}(F)\}
 =\frac1{N-1}\sum_{i=1}^N\left(Y_i^{\uparrow}(a)-\frac12\right)
 \left(Y_i^{\uparrow}(b)-\frac12\right)
 =\frac{N}{4(N-1)}.
\]
Reverse only arm \(b\).  The resulting \(Y\in\mathcal S_N(F)\) has
\[
 S_{ab}(Y)=-\frac{N}{4(N-1)},
\]
and all completion-dependent covariances involving another arm vanish.  Hence the exact identity above reduces to
\[
 \rho_W\{Y^{\uparrow}(F)\}-\rho_W(Y)
 =-\frac{2H_{ab}}N\frac{N}{2(N-1)}
 =-\frac{H_{ab}}{N-1}<0.
\]
Thus universal common-rank optimality fails.  This proves both directions and supplies the asserted finite binary counterexample.

Fix \(F\), \(Y\in\mathcal S_N(F)\), and write
\[
 D(Y)=\Sigma_C\{Y^{\uparrow}(F)\}-\Sigma_C(Y).
\]
The matrix \(D(Y)\) is symmetric, and therefore \(D(Y)\succeq0\) if and only if \(h^{\mathsf T}D(Y)h\geq0\) for every \(h\in\mathbb R^m\).  For a fixed \(h\), put \(v=C^{\mathsf T}h\).  The scalar estimator \(h^{\mathsf T}\widehat\tau=v^{\mathsf T}\widehat{\bar Y}\) has contrast Gram matrix
\[
 H_h=C^{\mathsf T}hh^{\mathsf T}C=vv^{\mathsf T}.
\]
Moreover, Assumption \(\mathrm{ass{:}causal\text{-}contrast}\) implies \(v^{\mathsf T}\mathbf 1_K=h^{\mathsf T}C\mathbf 1_K=0\).  Theorem \(\mathrm{thm{:}rank\text{-}cone\text{-}iff}\), applied to the one-dimensional contrast \(h^{\mathsf T}C\), consequently shows that universal Loewner dominance is equivalent to
\[
 v_av_b\leq0\quad\text{for every }a\ne b
 \quad\text{and every }v\in L:=\operatorname{range}(C^{\mathsf T}). \tag{1}
\]

We now classify the linear subspaces \(L\subseteq\mathbf 1_K^{\perp}\) satisfying (1).  Every nonzero \(v\in L\) has at most one positive coordinate and at most one negative coordinate.  Since its coordinates sum to zero, it follows that, for some unordered pair \(\{a,b\}\) and some \(t\ne0\),
\[
 v=t(e_a-e_b). \tag{2}
\]
All nonzero vectors in \(L\) must use the same unordered pair.  Indeed, if \(t(e_a-e_b)\) and \(s(e_c-e_d)\) have disjoint supports, their sum after choosing the signs of \(t,s\) has four nonzero coordinates and violates (1).  If their distinct supports share one coordinate, orienting and scaling them so that the shared coordinate has the same sign produces a linear combination with two coordinates of the opposite common sign, again violating (1).  Thus there is a fixed pair \(\{a,b\}\) such that
\[
 L\subseteq\operatorname{span}(e_a-e_b). \tag{3}
\]
Because \(C\ne0\), equality holds in (3).  Every row of \(C\) is therefore a multiple of \((e_a-e_b)^{\mathsf T}\), so there is a nonzero \(u\in\mathbb R^m\) with
\[
 C=u(e_a-e_b)^{\mathsf T}.
\]
Equivalently, column \(a\) is \(u\), column \(b\) is \(-u\), and all other columns vanish.

Conversely, if \(C=u(e_a-e_b)^{\mathsf T}\), then every \(v=C^{\mathsf T}h=(u^{\mathsf T}h)(e_a-e_b)\) satisfies (1).  Theorem \(\mathrm{thm{:}rank\text{-}cone\text{-}iff}\) gives \(h^{\mathsf T}D(Y)h\geq0\) for every \(h\), every admissible \(F\), and every completion \(Y\), hence \(D(Y)\succeq0\).

Finally, if \(C\) is not of the displayed two-column form, the proved subspace classification supplies \(h\) such that \(v=C^{\mathsf T}h\) has \(v_av_b>0\) for some pair.  The binary construction in the necessity part of Theorem \(\mathrm{thm{:}rank\text{-}cone\text{-}iff}\), with only those two arm marginals nonconstant, then gives
\[
 \operatorname{Var}_Z\!\left\{h^{\mathsf T}\widehat\tau\mid Y^{\uparrow}(F)\right\}
 -\operatorname{Var}_Z\!\left(h^{\mathsf T}\widehat\tau\mid Y\right)
 =-\frac{v_av_b}{N-1}<0.
\]
This is the required finite binary witness to failure of Loewner dominance.

For \(K=2\), \(C=(-1,1)\), and \(W=(1)\), direct multiplication gives
\[
 H=C^{\mathsf T}WC=
 \begin{pmatrix}1&-1\\-1&1\end{pmatrix}.
\]
This matrix is positive semidefinite, annihilates \(\mathbf 1_2\), and has nonpositive off-diagonal entries, hence \(H\in\mathcal R_2\) by Definition \(\mathrm{def{:}rank\text{-}cone}\).  Theorem \(\mathrm{thm{:}rank\text{-}cone\text{-}iff}\) therefore yields
\[
 \rho_1\{Y^{\uparrow}(F)\}=\sup_{Y\in\mathcal S_N(F)}
 \operatorname{Var}_Z\!\left\{\widehat{\bar Y}(2)-\widehat{\bar Y}(1)\mid Y\right\}.
\]
The proof of that theorem also shows directly that this supremum is obtained by maximizing \(S_{12}(Y)\), and the finite rearrangement calculation gives the maximizing covariance
\[
 \frac1{N-1}\sum_{i=1}^N
 \{Q_1(i/N)-\bar Y(1)\}\{Q_2(i/N)-\bar Y(2)\}.
\]
This is precisely the comonotone sharp upper randomization-variance endpoint: it optimizes over every joint finite schedule having the two prescribed empirical marginals, and the displayed common-rank schedule attains it.  Thus the general cone result reduces exactly to the stated two-arm endpoint.

Because the rows of \(C\) are an orthonormal basis of \(\mathbf 1_K^{\perp}\) and \(W=I_{K-1}\), the matrix
\[
 H=C^{\mathsf T}C
\]
is the orthogonal projector onto \(\mathbf 1_K^{\perp}\).  The orthogonal projector onto that subspace is uniquely
\[
 I_K-\frac1K\mathbf 1_K\mathbf 1_K^{\mathsf T}.
\]
Therefore \(H_{aa}=1-K^{-1}\) and \(H_{ab}=-K^{-1}\) for \(a\ne b\).  It follows directly from Definition \(\mathrm{def{:}rank\text{-}cone}\) that \(H\in\mathcal R_K\), and Theorem \(\mathrm{thm{:}rank\text{-}cone\text{-}iff}\) proves that common ranks maximize \(\operatorname{tr}\{\Sigma_C(Y)\}\), the sum of the randomization variances of the orthonormal contrasts.  If \(K>2\), then \(\operatorname{rank}(C)=K-1>1\), so \(C\) cannot have the two-column rank-one form characterized by Theorem \(\mathrm{thm{:}loewner\text{-}boundary}\).  Hence the scalar omnibus conclusion does not imply universal Loewner dominance.

The displayed rows of \(C\) sum to zero, and direct multiplication gives the displayed matrix \(H=C^{\mathsf T}C\).  It is positive semidefinite as a Gram matrix, satisfies \(H\mathbf 1_3=0\), and has off-diagonal entries \(-1,0,-1\); hence \(H\in\mathcal R_3\).

For \(q=(0,0,0,1,1,1)^{\mathsf T}\), the mean is \(1/2\), so
\[
 \frac1{N-1}\sum_{i=1}^6(q_i-1/2)^2
 =\frac15\,6\left(\frac14\right)=\frac3{10}.
\]
Thus the common-rank schedule has \(S_{ab}=3/10\) for all \(a,b\).  Lemma \(\mathrm{lem{:}complete\text{-}randomization\text{-}risk}\), together with \(n=2\) and \(H\mathbf 1_3=0\), gives
\[
 \rho_W\{Y^{\uparrow}(F)\}
 =\frac12(1+2+1)\frac3{10}
 -\frac16\frac3{10}\mathbf 1_3^{\mathsf T}H\mathbf 1_3
 =\frac35.
\]
Let \(\widetilde q=\mathbf 1_6-q\).  Then
\[
 \frac15\sum_{i=1}^6(q_i-1/2)(\widetilde q_i-1/2)=-\frac3{10}.
\]
The proposed schedule \((q,\widetilde q,q)\) therefore has \(S_{12}=S_{23}=-3/10\), \(S_{13}=3/10\), and diagonal variances \(3/10\).  Hence
\[
 \sum_{a,b=1}^3H_{ab}S_{ab}(Y)
 =4\frac3{10}+2\left\{(-1)\left(-\frac3{10}\right)+(-1)\left(-\frac3{10}\right)\right\}
 =\frac{12}{5},
\]
and the risk identity gives
\[
 \rho_W(Y)=\frac35-\frac16\frac{12}{5}=\frac15.
\]
Equivalently, the exact regret formula of Theorem \(\mathrm{thm{:}rank\text{-}cone\text{-}iff}\) yields
\[
 \rho_W\{Y^{\uparrow}(F)\}-\rho_W(Y)
 =\frac13\left\{\frac3{10}-\left(-\frac3{10}\right)
 +\frac3{10}-\left(-\frac3{10}\right)\right\}=\frac25.
\]
Every displayed column contains three zeros and three ones, so both schedules belong to \(\mathcal S_6(F)\).

Writing \(c=(1,1,-2)^{\mathsf T}\), we have \(H=cc^{\mathsf T}\), which is positive semidefinite and satisfies \(H\mathbf 1_3=0\).  Its entry \(H_{12}=1>0\), so Definition \(\mathrm{def{:}rank\text{-}cone}\) gives \(H\notin\mathcal R_3\).

Let \(q=(0,0,0,1,1,1)^{\mathsf T}\).  As computed in the preceding proposition, its finite-population variance is \(3/10\).  Under the common-rank schedule \((q,q,0)\),
\[
 S_{11}=S_{22}=S_{12}=\frac3{10},
\]
and every covariance involving arm \(3\) is zero.  Lemma \(\mathrm{lem{:}complete\text{-}randomization\text{-}risk}\) gives
\[
 \rho_W\{Y^{\uparrow}(F)\}
 =\frac12\left(\frac3{10}+\frac3{10}\right)
 -\frac16\left(\frac3{10}+\frac3{10}+2\frac3{10}\right)
 =\frac1{10}.
\]
Reverse only the second column, using \(\widetilde q=\mathbf 1_6-q\).  The resulting schedule remains in \(\mathcal S_6(F)\), has \(S_{11}=S_{22}=3/10\) and \(S_{12}=-3/10\), and therefore
\[
 \rho_W(Y)
 =\frac3{10}-\frac16\left(\frac3{10}+\frac3{10}-2\frac3{10}\right)
 =\frac3{10}.
\]
The exact regret is consequently
\[
 \rho_W\{Y^{\uparrow}(F)\}-\rho_W(Y)
 =\frac13(-1)\left\{\frac3{10}-\left(-\frac3{10}\right)\right\}
 =-\frac15<0.
\]
This verifies every claimed covariance and loss and supplies a feasible finite binary witness.

added_lemmas.statement:
Let \(H\in\mathbb S_+^K\) and \(\Omega\in\mathfrak K^{\mathrm{bal}}_{N,K}\).  Put \(J=\mathcal A\times\{1,\ldots,N-1\}\).  For \(\pi\in\mathfrak S_N\) and \(\sigma\in\mathfrak S_N^K\), define the symmetric \(|J|\times|J|\) matrix \(B^{\pi,\sigma}\) by
\[
 B^{\pi,\sigma}_{(a,r),(b,s)}
 =\frac{H_{ab}}{N^2}\sum_{i,j=1}^N\Omega_{ab,\pi(i),\pi(j)}
 \left[(d_r)_i(d_s)_j-(d_r)_{\sigma_a(i)}(d_s)_{\sigma_b(j)}\right].
\]
Then \(\Omega^\pi\in\mathcal C_{N,K}(H)\) if and only if \(B^{\pi,\sigma}\) is copositive for every \(\sigma\), meaning \(u^{\mathsf T}B^{\pi,\sigma}u\geq0\) for every \(u\in\mathbb R_+^J\).  Consequently,
\[
 [\Omega]_{\cong}\in\mathfrak C^{\mathrm{bal}}_{N,K}(H)
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 \text{there exists }\pi\in\mathfrak S_N\text{ such that every }B^{\pi,\sigma}\text{ is copositive}.
\]
For any real symmetric matrix \(B\) indexed by \(J\), copositivity has the finite support characterization
\[
 B\text{ is copositive}
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 \ker\{B[I]-\lambda I_I\}\cap\mathbb R_{++}^{I}=\varnothing
\]
for every nonempty \(I\subseteq J\) and every negative real eigenvalue \(\lambda<0\) of the principal matrix \(B[I]\).

If, in addition, the entries of \(H\) and \(\Omega\) are supplied as exact real-algebraic numbers, in particular as rational numbers, these equivalences give a finite exact recognition algorithm.  It enumerates \(\pi\), \(\sigma\), and nonempty \(I\), isolates every negative algebraic eigenvalue of \(B^{\pi,\sigma}[I]\), and decides by exact ordered-field linear feasibility whether its eigenspace meets \(\mathbb R_{++}^{I}\).  A noncopositivity certificate consists of \((I,\lambda,v)\) with \(v\in\ker\{B^{\pi,\sigma}[I]-\lambda I_I\}\cap\mathbb R_{++}^{I}\); it yields explicit ordered columns with at most \(N\) levels and a strict loss improvement.  A certificate that a fixed \(\pi\) works consists of the finite collection of infeasibility certificates for all these negative-eigenspace tests.  Thus a yes instance returns such a \(\pi\), while a no instance returns, for every \(\pi\), a corresponding strict cut witness.  No algebraic enumeration claim is made for unrestricted real inputs, and the exhaustive algorithm is not asserted to run in polynomial time.
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
Fix \(\pi\) and \(\sigma\).  Every \(x^a\in\mathcal M_N\) has the unique adjacent-increment representation
\[
 x^a=x_1^a\mathbf 1_N+\sum_{r=1}^{N-1}\alpha_{ar}d_r,
 \qquad \alpha_{ar}=x^a_{r+1}-x^a_r\geq0.
\]
By Definition \(\mathrm{def{:}admissible\text{-}balanced\text{-}kernel}\), \(\sum_i\Omega_{abij}=\sum_j\Omega_{abij}=0\).  These identities are preserved by the common relabelling \(\pi\), so every term containing a constant vector vanishes from both \(\mathscr L_{H,\Omega^\pi}(x,\mathrm{id})\) and \(\mathscr L_{H,\Omega^\pi}(x,\sigma)\).  Substitution of the increment representations into Definition \(\mathrm{def{:}balanced\text{-}kernel\text{-}loss}\) gives, exactly,
\[
 \mathscr L_{H,\Omega^\pi}(x,\mathrm{id})
 -\mathscr L_{H,\Omega^\pi}(x,\sigma)
 =\sum_{(a,r),(b,s)\in J}\alpha_{ar}
 B^{\pi,\sigma}_{(a,r),(b,s)}\alpha_{bs}
 =\alpha^{\mathsf T}B^{\pi,\sigma}\alpha. \tag{4}
\]
The covariance symmetry \(\Omega_{abij}=\Omega_{baji}\), symmetry of \(H\), and interchange of \((a,r,i)\) with \((b,s,j)\) show that \(B^{\pi,\sigma}\) is symmetric.  Conversely, every \(\alpha\in\mathbb R_+^J\) defines ordered columns by taking \(x_1^a=0\) and the displayed cumulative sums.  Therefore (4) proves
\[
 \mathscr L_{H,\Omega^\pi}(x,\mathrm{id})\geq
 \mathscr L_{H,\Omega^\pi}(x,\sigma)\text{ for every }x
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 B^{\pi,\sigma}\text{ is copositive}.
\]
Taking the conjunction over the finite set \(\mathfrak S_N^K\), then the disjunction over \(\pi\in\mathfrak S_N\), proves the first two assertions from Definitions \(\mathrm{def{:}identity\text{-}optimal\text{-}kernel\text{-}cone}\), \(\mathrm{def{:}unit\text{-}relabeling\text{-}equivalence}\), and \(\mathrm{def{:}admissible\text{-}rank\text{-}kernel\text{-}domain}\).

It remains to prove the support criterion.  If a principal matrix \(B[I]\) has \(B[I]v=\lambda v\) for \(\lambda<0\) and \(v\in\mathbb R_{++}^I\), extending \(v\) by zero outside \(I\) gives a nonnegative vector \(\widetilde v\) with
\[
 \widetilde v^{\mathsf T}B\widetilde v
 =v^{\mathsf T}B[I]v=\lambda\lVert v\rVert_2^2<0,
\]
so \(B\) is not copositive.

Conversely, suppose \(B\) is not copositive.  The compact set
\[
 \mathcal D=\{u\in\mathbb R_+^J:\lVert u\rVert_2=1\}
\]
contains a minimizer \(u^*\) of the continuous function \(u\mapsto u^{\mathsf T}Bu\), and its minimum \(\lambda=(u^*)^{\mathsf T}Bu^*\) is negative.  Let \(I=\{j:u_j^*>0\}\).  The vector \(u_I^*\) lies in the relative interior of the positive orthant on the unit sphere in \(\mathbb R^I\).  For every \(w\in\mathbb R^I\) with \(w^{\mathsf T}u_I^*=0\), both signs of a sufficiently small tangent perturbation remain positive on \(I\); first-order minimality therefore gives
\[
 w^{\mathsf T}B[I]u_I^*=0.
\]
Thus \(B[I]u_I^*\) is parallel to \(u_I^*\).  Taking the inner product with \(u_I^*\) identifies the multiplier as \(\lambda<0\), so
\[
 B[I]u_I^*=\lambda u_I^*,
 \qquad u_I^*\in\mathbb R_{++}^I.
\]
This proves the equivalence using every negative real eigenvalue, not merely the sign of the spectrum of the full matrix.

Under the additional exact real-algebraic input hypothesis, every entry of every \(B^{\pi,\sigma}[I]\), every coefficient of its characteristic polynomial, and every eigenvalue is real algebraic.  Passing the finitely many input numbers to a common primitive-element representation, square-free factorization followed by exact sign-variation bisection produces disjoint rational isolating intervals for every real root; exact sign determination then identifies all negative eigenvalues.  Every operation is an exact field operation or a sign test on an algebraic number, and degrees decrease in the Euclidean remainder sequence, so this root-isolation procedure terminates.  For a fixed negative eigenvalue \(\lambda\), homogeneity gives
\[
 \ker\{B[I]-\lambda I_I\}\cap\mathbb R_{++}^I\ne\varnothing
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 \exists v:\ (B[I]-\lambda I_I)v=0,\quad v_j\geq1\ (j\in I). \tag{5}
\]
Indeed, a strictly positive vector can be scaled by the reciprocal of its smallest coordinate, and the reverse implication is immediate.  The right side of (5) is a finite linear-feasibility problem over an ordered field of real algebraic numbers.  Eliminate equalities by exact Gaussian operations, and then eliminate each remaining variable by pairing every lower affine bound with every upper affine bound.  Each elimination produces finitely many inequalities and preserves feasibility in both directions; induction on the number of variables reduces the question to finitely many exact sign tests.  Back-substitution returns a feasible algebraic vector, while the incompatible lower--upper pairings give an exact infeasibility certificate.  Since the sets of \(\pi\), \(\sigma\), \(I\), and eigenvalues are finite, the stated algorithm terminates.

When (5) is feasible, extend \(v\) by zero to \(\alpha\in\mathbb R_+^J\) and set
\[
 x_i^a=\sum_{r<i}\alpha_{ar}.
\]
Each column is ordered and has no more than \(N\) distinct values.  Equations (4) and (5) yield
\[
 \mathscr L_{H,\Omega^\pi}(x,\mathrm{id})
 -\mathscr L_{H,\Omega^\pi}(x,\sigma)
 =\lambda\lVert v\rVert_2^2<0,
\]
which is the promised exact strict witness.  Exhausting all tests gives the stated yes and no certificates.  The enumeration includes \((N!)^{K+1}(2^{K(N-1)}-1)\) permutation-support combinations before eigenvalue multiplicities are counted, so this proof supplies only a finite exact algorithm and makes no polynomial-time claim.

proposed.statement: Fix \(N\), \(K\), and \(H=C^{\mathsf T}WC\), and restrict the input to a rational tensor \(\Omega\in\mathfrak K^{\mathrm{bal}}_{N,K}\), supplied either with its exact entries or by a rational law \(p\in\mathfrak P^{\mathrm{bal}}_{N,K}\) inducing those entries. Characterize the cone \(\mathcal C_{N,K}(H)\) on this feasible domain and hence the label-free set \(\mathfrak C^{\mathrm{bal}}_{N,K}(H)\): equivalently, decide whether some common unit relabelling \(\pi\in\mathfrak S_N\) makes \(\mathscr L_{H,\Omega^{\pi}}(x,\mathrm{id})\geq\mathscr L_{H,\Omega^{\pi}}(x,\sigma)\) for every \(x\in\mathcal M_N^K\) and every \(\sigma\in\mathfrak S_N^K\). Derive a recognition algorithm polynomial in \(N\), \(K\), and the rational input bit length that returns such a relabelling and a finite cut certificate on yes instances, and returns arm-specific binary ordered columns together with \(\sigma\) giving a strict exact loss improvement on no instances; if binary separation is not complete, characterize the minimal finite alphabet required for a complete separating certificate.
proposed.justification: The feasible moment-polytope domain separates genuine randomization kernels from arbitrary four-index arrays and turns universal rank preservation into a label-invariant decision problem.
proposed.gap: An exact finite copositivity characterization is available, but a polynomial-time recognition algorithm and a complete minimal-alphabet failure certificate remain unresolved.
proposed.consumer: The exact characterization supports auditable small-design recognition; a scalable certificate for matched, paired, rerandomized, and geographically balanced experiments remains the open deliverable.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The complete-randomization rank-cone theorem is not used by the general balanced-kernel question or its cut-copositivity characterization, so the stale dependency is removed as directed.

open_obligations.what_is_open: Construct an algorithm polynomial in \(N\), \(K\), and rational input bit length for orbit membership in \(\mathfrak C^{\mathrm{bal}}_{N,K}(H)\), with the requested relabelling and finite yes certificate and a binary no witness; alternatively prove a faithful complexity obstruction on the admissible balanced moment-polytope image. If binary witnesses are not complete, determine the least uniform finite alphabet size that is complete.
open_obligations.obstruction: The proved characterization enumerates \(N!\) common relabellings, \((N!)^K\) arm permutations, all nonempty principal supports in dimension \(K(N-1)\), and their negative eigenspaces. This is finite and exact but not polynomial. A negative cut quadratic form may use several positive adjacent increments in one arm, so the copositivity witness need not be binary. No reduction or structural theorem has been established that either exploits the balanced covariance-moment constraints to remove these enumerations or proves they are unavoidable.
open_obligations.attempted: Expanded every monotone column in suffix cuts, reduced identity-optimality to explicit copositivity matrices, and reduced noncopositivity to exact strict-positive-eigenspace feasibility over all principal supports. Single-cut inspection was also considered, but mixed cut products in the quadratic form prevent reduction of a general negative witness to one cut per arm.
open_obligations.partial_result: For every real admissible \(\Omega\), the orbit-membership question is equivalent to the existence of a relabelling \(\pi\) for which finitely many explicit cut matrices \(B^{\pi,\sigma}\) are copositive.  Copositivity of each matrix is equivalent to the absence, for every nonempty principal support and every negative real eigenvalue, of a strictly positive vector in the corresponding eigenspace.  With exact real-algebraic inputs this yields a terminating exact root-isolation and ordered-field linear-feasibility algorithm, together with exact multilevel cut witnesses on failure.  The algorithm is exhaustive rather than polynomial, and its witnesses can require up to \(N\) levels per arm.

prose_updates.tldr: Under balanced complete randomization, the common-rank potential-outcome completion is universally least favourable for the scalarized covariance loss \(\operatorname{tr}\{W\operatorname{Cov}_Z(C\widehat{\bar Y})\}\) if and only if the contrast Gram matrix \(H=C^{\mathsf T}WC\) is a graph Laplacian. This gives an \(O(K^2)\) certificate, exact six-unit audit examples, and a binary counterexample outside the cone. Common ranks dominate the entire multi-contrast covariance matrix only for a vector-rescaled pairwise contrast. For a general admissible balanced covariance tensor, cut expansion gives an exact finite copositivity characterization and, for exact real-algebraic inputs, an exhaustive root-isolation and linear-feasibility algorithm. Polynomial-time recognition and the minimal complete failure-witness alphabet remain open.

project_justification.gap: Sharp rank completion is analytic for the two-arm difference-in-means estimator, whereas generalized causal-bootstrap work uses integer programming for broad designs and estimators. The literature does not state the exact contrast-geometry boundary at which one common-rank completion remains universally least favourable in a multi-arm experiment. On the realizable nonexchangeable balanced-kernel domain, the remaining gap is a polynomial-time recognition method, or a faithful hardness result, together with a minimal-alphabet separating certificate.
project_justification.niche: The object is neither a generic transport solver nor another conservative covariance estimator. It is a design-computable graph-Laplacian cone for complete randomization, a sharper classification for joint covariance dominance, and an exact cut-copositivity representation on the admissible balanced moment polytope modulo common unit relabelling.
project_justification.fill: The project derives the complete-randomization risk decomposition, proves the graph-Laplacian equivalence by finite rearrangement and isolated binary necessity witnesses, evaluates both mechanisms exactly at \(K=3,N=6\), and classifies the Loewner case. For general balanced kernels it proves that identity-optimality is equivalent to copositivity of finitely many explicit cut matrices and supplies a terminating exact algebraic algorithm with multilevel witnesses, while leaving polynomial complexity and the minimal complete alphabet as explicit residual questions.

prose_updates.related_work: Aronow, Green, and Lee establish the two-arm comonotone sharp endpoint, which the two-arm proposition recovers exactly. Imbens and Menzel use the same isotone completion to obtain a least-favourable limiting experiment. Zhao and Ding supply the arbitrary-contrast complete-randomization covariance identity but do not optimize its unidentified cross-arm terms. Tchen's supermodular-order theorem is consistent with the pairwise rearrangement mechanism, while the proof here gives the needed finite permutation argument directly. Gao, Ge, and Qian formulate general quadratic cross-world extrema as multi-marginal transport, and Brennan et al. compute generalized causal-bootstrap completions by integer programming. The present general-kernel theorem instead restricts to covariance tensors in the exact finite moment-polytope image of balanced assignment laws and gives a finite cut-copositivity characterization. Laurent and Seminaroti's Robinson--Toeplitz result concerns a sufficient identity-optimal class for a two-matrix quadratic assignment problem; it does not supply the necessary-and-sufficient or polynomial recognition result sought here.
prose_updates.interpretation: For complete randomization, a practitioner needs only inspect the off-diagonal signs of \(C^{\mathsf T}WC\): nonpositive signs certify one-sort least-favourable completion, while any positive sign identifies two arms on which a binary reversal strictly improves the loss. Matrix-valued conservativeness is much rarer and occurs only for a rescaled single pairwise contrast. Under a nonexchangeable balanced design, the analogous exact question is a finite family of copositivity tests after choosing a common unit order; this is mathematically decidable for exact algebraic inputs but is not yet a scalable certificate.
prose_updates.technical_internal_limitation: The graph-Laplacian certificate concerns a prespecified scalar covariance loss \(W\) and does not turn that endpoint into a sharp matrix-valued covariance bound. Except for a rescaled pairwise contrast, no single common-rank completion dominates every linear combination simultaneously. For general balanced kernels, the copositivity theorem is an exhaustive finite characterization: it enumerates factorially many relabellings and arm permutations and exponentially many supports, and its strict witnesses may have as many as \(N\) ordered levels per arm. It therefore does not satisfy the open polynomial-time or binary-certificate requirement.
prose_updates.honest_scope: The complete-randomization cone theorem follows from the design covariance identity plus a finite rearrangement proof and a new contrast-geometry necessity classification; novelty lies in the causal contrast cone and Loewner boundary, not in a new general dependence inequality. The six-unit propositions are audit certificates rather than asymptotic claims. The general balanced-kernel contribution is presently the exact cut-copositivity equivalence and a terminating algorithm only for exact real-algebraic inputs. No algebraic enumeration is claimed for unrestricted real inputs, and no polynomial runtime, hardness classification, binary completeness, or minimal-alphabet theorem is claimed.

statement_notes.justification: The theorem gives the computable side of the nonexchangeable extension: universal monotone-column inequalities reduce exactly to finitely many principal-eigenspace feasibility tests.
statement_notes.gap: Its exhaustive algorithm does not establish polynomial complexity, and its multilevel failure witnesses do not settle binary completeness or the least complete alphabet.
statement_notes.consumer: Small balanced designs with exact rational kernels can be audited exactly, with a relabelling certificate on success or explicit ordered columns and an improving permutation on failure.

statement_notes.justification: The residual question isolates computational structure after the feasible-domain mathematics has been characterized exactly.
statement_notes.gap: Polynomial-time recognition or a faithful hardness result, together with binary completeness or a minimal-alphabet characterization, remains open.
statement_notes.consumer: A solution would turn the current exact but exhaustive audit into a scalable design certificate with standardized failure witnesses.
